   476→/**

   479→export function generateOutfits(
   480→  products: Product[],
   481→  options: {
   482→    count?: number
   483→    style?: OutfitStyle
   484→    gender?: 'men' | 'women'
   485→    priceRange?: { min: number; max: number }
   486→  } = {}
   487→): Outfit[] {
   488→  const { count = 5, style = 'any', gender, priceRange } = options
   489→
   490→  // Filter by gender if specified
   491→  let filteredProducts = gender ? filterProductsByGender(products, gender) : products
   492→
   493→  // Filter by price range if specified
   494→  if (priceRange) {
   495→    filteredProducts = filteredProducts.filter(
   496→      (p) => p.price >= priceRange.min && p.price <= priceRange.max
   497→    )
   498→  }
   499→
   500→  // Filter out out-of-stock products
   501→  filteredProducts = filteredProducts.filter((p) => p.availability !== 'out_of_stock')
   502→
   503→  // Filter by style/occasion if products have tags
   504→  if (style && style !== 'any') {
   505→    const targetOccasion = style === 'business' ? 'work' : style;
   506→    // Only filter if the product HAS an occasion tag. If not, assume it's versatile (mock Central products usually versatile).
   507→    // Actually, for better accuracy, let's filter those that DO have tags.
   508→    // SFERA items have tags. Central mocks don't.
   509→    // If I enforce strict filtering, Central items (without tags) might disappear if they are not compatible?
   510→    // Let's check matching.
   511→    filteredProducts = filteredProducts.filter(p => {
   512→      if (!p.occasion || p.occasion.length === 0) return true; // Keep products without tags (generic)
   513→      return p.occasion.some(occ => occ === targetOccasion || occ === style);
   514→    });
   515→  }
   516→
   517→  const categorized = categorizeProducts(filteredProducts)
   518→  const outfits: Outfit[] = []
   519→  const usedCombinations = new Set<string>() // Track used product combinations
   520→
   521→  // Try to generate requested number of outfits
   522→  let attempts = 0
   523→  const maxAttempts = count * 5 // Increased attempts to find uniques
   524→
   525→  const usedPrimarySkus = new Set<string>()
   526→
   527→  while (outfits.length < count && attempts < maxAttempts) {
   528→    const outfit = generateOutfit(categorized, style, gender)
   529→    if (outfit && outfit.items.length > 0) {
   530→      // Create a unique signature for this outfit based on product SKUs
   531→      const signature = outfit.items.map(p => p.sku).sort().join('-')
   532→      const primarySku = outfit.items[0].sku // Assume first item is primary (Top/Dress)
   533→
   534→      // Check if we've already used this combination OR this primary item
   535→      if (!usedCombinations.has(signature) && !usedPrimarySkus.has(primarySku)) {
   536→        // Check if outfit fits price range
   537→        if (!priceRange || (outfit.totalPrice >= priceRange.min && outfit.totalPrice <= priceRange.max)) {
   538→          outfits.push(outfit)
   539→          usedCombinations.add(signature)
   540→          usedPrimarySkus.add(primarySku)
   541→        }
   542→      }
   543→    }
   544→    attempts++
   545→  }
   546→
   547→  return outfits
   548→}

# OOTDay - AI Fashion Assistant

An AI-powered fashion assistant platform that helps users with daily outfit decisions and connects fashion inspiration directly to purchase opportunities.

## Overview

OOTDay combines:
- **AI Chat Interface**: Natural language fashion recommendations powered by Claude AI
- **Product Matching**: Integration with Central Group inventory for direct purchases
- **Multi-Agent Development**: Automated task processing with parallel Claude Code agents

cd apps/web

/**

  | 'polka-dot'
  | 'geometric'
  | 'abstract'
  | 'animal-print'

// Brand Positioning Tier
export type BrandTier = 'budget' | 'mid-range' | 'premium' | 'luxury'

// Outfit Role

  | 'bottom'
  | 'dress'
  | 'outerwear'

  | 'blend'
